title: Automated reading of TLC plates — Problem Statement (Mstack Chemicals, prepared by Tejas Ghatule)
two_line_summary:
In-house 7-page problem statement defining the system's inputs (4-lane S/Co/R/Sd plates under UV 254 nm with handwritten metadata), the five signals to read, and the decision outputs (complete/stalled/progressing, conversion estimate, by-product flags).
Binding for product requirements the measurement brief doesn't carry: lane semantics, decision rules (ΔSM≈0 and Δproduct≈0 across ~2 intervals = stalled), and stated scope limits — but its Rf-with-solvent-front framing is superseded by the brief's Rst finding.
key_points: Plate format: 4 lanes labeled S (starting material reference), Co (other reactants reference), R (reaction mixture — the lane actually read), Sd (authentic product standard); labels handwritten under lanes at bottom edge (p2-3)
Metadata handwritten on every plate: reaction ID (e.g. MEHQ-P31), time sampled (e.g. 4 hr), mobile phase (e.g. 30% EA-Hex), imaged under UV 254 nm (p2)

Five signals to extract: (1) spot position/Rf, (2) spot count = purity/by-products, (3) intensity = amount / % conversion, (4) match vs Sd lane height = product confirmed, (5) shape & baseline (streaks = overload/decomposition; origin spots = polar residue) (p4)
Required outputs: which spot is which, SM left in R lane, product formed, extra spots flagged, complete/incomplete call, conversion estimate, by-product warning — 'same call every time' (p1)

Decision logic per plate: PROGRESSING = SM falling & product rising -> continue; STALLED = no change across ~2 consecutive intervals with SM still present (ΔSM≈0 and Δproduct≈0) -> intervene; COMPLETE = SM spot gone or below limit -> quench (p6)
System must work with single end-point plates (~4 hr today) AND interval series; example curve: ~86% product, ~12% SM at 240 min; stall example plateaus at ~55% product (p5-6)
Archive plates referenced: P31 4hr, P32 4+3hr (same format two timepoints), P30 4hr, P32-1 3hr in ACN — P32 gives a real two-timepoint series (p3)
Motivating gap: visual reads subjective (two chemists quote 50% vs 70% from same plate), qualitative, unrecorded (p1)

Stated limits (p7): same Rf does not prove identity (Sd match is evidence, not proof; MS/NMR confirms); UV 254 only shows conjugated compounds — imaging condition (UV/stain) must be part of each plate's data; Rf drifts day-to-day so only same-plate comparisons are rigorous (why reference lanes ride on every plate); results are semi-quantitative, for in-process decisions, not release certificates — HPLC owns final purity/yield
Scope boundary: automate the read-out only; chemistry stays with the chemist (p1)
Prior art cited: TLCyzer (Nature Sci. Reports 2022), MIA-TLC reaction monitoring (p7)

SUPERSEDED DETAIL: doc's schematic assumes a visible solvent front and Rf = spot distance / solvent distance (p2, p4); the binding brief established real plates show no solvent front, so Rst (vs reference spot) replaces Rf
deep_read_reason: Full text already extracted (7 pages, text-only); all concrete requirements are captured above — remaining content is figures/illustrations.

title: Reading a TLC plate — Mstack Chemicals (6-page landscape brief)
two_line_summary:
Market/landscape brief: measuring TLC plates from photos is solved commodity work (30+ tools since 2007), while naming spots in reaction context is the empty niche nobody sells.
Concludes measurement and naming must be done by separate components (classical CV measures, language model names) — consistent with the binding brief, adding competitive context rather than build parameters.
key_points: Rf defined as spot distance / solvent-front distance, range 0-1; a chemist reads a plate in ~5 seconds (p.1)
30+ distinct photo-to-chromatogram tools exist since 2007 (first was a high-school project, TLC Analyzer); best has ~1,000 installs worldwide; zero identify what a spot IS (p.2)

Prior tools' universal pipeline: (1) find lanes almost always by hand, (2) collapse each lane column-by-column into a curve, (3) user-guessed cutoff threshold, (4) report position+darkness, never a name (p.3)

Six hardware tiers: bare phone (uncontrolled), phone + UV 254 nm box ($36-78 in parts), flatbed scanner, imaging cabinet (254/366 nm + white, fixed geometry), slit densitometer (PMT, no camera), robot+fixed camera (4,944 published measurements, no images) (p.3)
Phone-based measurement gets within 2-5% of a densitometer but is 15-30x less sensitive - rarely matters for reaction monitoring (p.6)

On the project's own plates: OCR/VLM read handwritten lane labels 0 of 14 correct; classical software found 6 of 6 spots (VLM misses faint ones, drifts); VLM correctly names the product given reaction context (p.5) - matches binding brief findings
Architectural conclusion: measuring and naming should NOT be done by the same component - vision models describe brilliantly and measure badly (p.5)

Cautionary field-trial result: the one large automated plate-reading trial raised bad-medicine detection from 35% to 62.5% but dropped specificity to 75.2% (1 in 4 good medicines flagged); its authors concluded it was not fit to deploy (p.6)
No public dataset of labelled plate images exists; no object-detection paper for TLC spots exists (p.6)

Watch items: gauge-reading VLM benchmark went 30% to 42% in under a year; CAMAG AI add-on released Feb 2026 (first commercial product above measurement, classifies whole samples not spots); ~$4bn invested in reaction robots in 18 months, none use TLC as a sensor (NMR/HPLC/MS instead) (p.6)
deep_read_reason: All six pages were fully extracted and indexed; the document is a short positioning brief with no technical parameters beyond what is captured in key_points, and its findings align with (rather than extend) the binding brief.

title: Reading a TLC plate — Seventeen questions, answered with evidence rather than opinion (Mstack Chemicals research report, by Tejas Ghatule)
two_line_summary:
In-house 21-page survey of the TLC-image-reading field (30+ prior tools since 2007) concluding measurement is commodity and spot NAMING in reaction context is the gap; prescribes the exact split the build follows: deterministic pixel-level measurement, LLM interpretation from a numbers table only.
Carries the acceptance criteria (9/10 blind-chemist agreement, <5% false alarms, photo-only input) and the measurement-to-LLM handover schema (lane, Rf, OD, share of lane, SNR, confidence) — items the 15-finding brief may not restate.
key_points: Q15 (p18) architecture mandate: measurement layer deterministic (no model, no sampling, same photo -> same numbers); LLM works ONLY from a handover table, never the image; handover schema: lane, Rf, optical density, share of lane, signal-to-noise, confidence per spot
Q15: if confidence is low anywhere, system must say so and ask the chemist rather than guess; every number traceable back to pixels

Q17 (p20) success criteria: agree with blind chemist on 9/10 uncurated plates; false-alarm rate below 5% (the metric the 2024 Nigeria field trial failed on — specificity, not sensitivity); effort = one photograph and nothing else typed 'or it will not be used'

Q17 validation protocol: random uncurated archive plates including badly photographed ones, chemist records blind verdict BEFORE seeing system output, report every failure, lead results with false alarms; 4-week plan (pull archive / blind read / run+compare / hostile-user trial)

Q6 (p9) accuracy numbers: phone+free-software LOD 3-35 ug/spot vs scanning densitometer 0.2-1 ug (15-30x less sensitive); both <2% relative deviation, 98-102% recovery; TLCyzer 2022 smartphone precision 4.46% in lab, 8.4% median / 16.4% mean deviation vs HPLC in 2024 Nigeria field trial

Q6 Rf variability (IAEA inter-lab study): within-lab relative deviation <20% (worse below Rf 0.2); in band Rf 0.3-0.7 variation <0.1; between labs mostly <11% but up to 31%; conclusion: position vs a reference on the SAME plate is far more stable than absolute Rf — supports the brief's Rst approach (note: report's general framing assumes a solvent front, which the brief supersedes for MEHQ plates)

Q6: Porto group lane/band-detection algorithm literature — wavelet smoothing of intensity profile + morphological candidate detection + validation by lane width/spacing/intensity; tested on 66 images/651 lanes and 169 images/1,422 lanes; known failure: discards top quarter of image

Q10 (p13) own-plate benchmark matching the brief: OCR of handwritten lane labels 0/14 crops for every classical engine vs all-correct for VLM; classical found 6/6 verified features on hardest plate while VLM misses faint spots and positions drift; VLM gives no calibrated quantity but correctly names product given lane context

Q10 gauge-reading benchmark: frontier-model best 30.2% (Oct 2025) -> 41.7% today, one frontier model at 7.5% — measurement by VLM not solved; measurement code is 'a few hundred lines of arithmetic' designed to be swappable

Q11 (p14): no public labelled TLC plate image dataset exists (HuggingFace/Kaggle/Roboflow/Zenodo all empty); no YOLO/U-Net/segmentation paper on TLC spots exists; only 4 NN-on-plate-image works (earliest 2018 Fichou & Morlock; 2024 GAN+CNN ginger species 98.7% on 77 real images)

Q5 (p8): all prior software shares 3 flaws to avoid — human does the geometry, a user-chosen threshold changes the answer, output is a number never a name; qTLC (UCL 2018) reported 2.6-3.8% error with user-picked peak-height cutoff

Q2/Q3 framing: 4-level ladder (geometry, quantification, interpretation, decision); build targets full 1-2-3 plus proposed 4; chemist does all four in ~5 seconds — value of automating 1-2 alone for a human bench is near zero; darkness-quantity relation is an optical law but NOT linear in raw pixel value

Kill criteria (p20): stop if a chemist by eye matches the system faster; if a frontier vision model measures as well as the pipeline; or if autonomous platforms settle on benchtop NMR/inline analytics instead of TLC

Market findings (p1, p4): 30+ existing free/cheap tools all stop at spot-finding; zero products name spots; ~$4B recently invested in reaction-running robots that cannot read a plate — the target buyer
deep_read_reason: Key technical pages (architecture, accuracy tables, VLM benchmarks, success criteria) already extracted; remaining pages are market/pricing/buyer analysis (Q7-Q9, Q13-Q14, Q16) and a source list, none of which constrain the build. The report predates and is partly restated by the binding brief; only the Q15 handover schema and Q17 acceptance numbers warrant carrying into specs if the brief lacks them.

title: Running TLC the right way — Mstack Chemicals TLC Standard Operating Practice
two_line_summary:
Internal 7-page SOP (by Tejas Ghatule) with 14 numbered bench/photo rules, each traced to a defective MEHQ/Reaction_test1 plate, plus a one-page checklist and a "what software can/cannot fix" table.
Confirms the brief's world (missing solvent fronts, uneven loading, bad photos) and defines what FUTURE input images will look like — useful for input validation and QC checks, not new measurement algorithms.
key_points: Origin line: pencil, ~1.5 cm from bottom edge, drawn before spotting; lane labels pencil-written under the origin line (rule 1, p2)

Solvent front must be pencil-marked within seconds of removing plate; unmarked front is unrecoverable by software — no edge/tint/texture remains, so Rf is permanently lost (rules 2, p2 + p7 table). All existing MEHQ plates miss it — consistent with brief's Rst-not-Rf finding
Origin line CAN be partly recovered by software: fit a line through visible spotting dots; degrades on messy/streaked plates (P32 cited) (p2)
Spotting: same capillary, same number of touches per lane (e.g. 2x), dry between touches; spots <=3-4 mm diameter (rule 3, p3)
Spacing: >=8 mm between spots, >=10 mm from each plate edge (rule 5, p3); E-30min plate shows S spot bleeding into A2 lane from tight spacing

Reference lanes (S and Std) must be loaded to intensity comparable to reaction lanes; MEHQ-P33 Std lane too faint to anchor comparison (rule 4, p3) — under-loaded reference is listed as never software-fixable (p7)
Overloading streaks (T-30, E-30 plates: full-length streaks in every reaction lane) destroy position and intensity info; never software-fixable (rule 6, p3; p7 table)
Development: filter-paper-lined saturated chamber ~5-10 min, lid on, solvent below origin; stop run when front is ~1 cm from top (rules 7-8, p4)
Plate metadata format written above front line: 'MEHQ-P34 - 60 min - 30% EA-Hex' (reaction ID - timepoint - mobile phase); filename must equal plate header, e.g. MEHQ-P34_T_30min.jpg (rules 9, 14)
Target Rf 0.3-0.5 for compound of interest; S and Std must visibly separate — on all three 30-min screening plates they co-run at nearly the same height (rule 10, p4)

Photo spec: phone JPEG in UV-254 cabinet, no RAW/DNG (45 MB DNGs 'add nothing'), no flash, no zoom; straight-on 90-degree view; plate fills ~60-80% of frame; origin at bottom; both lines + all labels + header must be in frame, no cropping (rules 11-13, p5)

Cited validation: TLCyzer study (Nature Scientific Reports 2022) — ~100% mean accuracy, ~3% repeatability from ordinary phone JPEGs; phone-camera TLC validated for drug-authenticity screening (J. Pharm. Biomed. Anal. 2016) (p1, p5)
Optional (not required): phone tripod in front of UV box; exposure lock (long-press on iPhone) to keep brightness comparable across a series (p5) — relevant to the brief's exposure-clipping finding

Software fixability table (p7): rotation trivially fixable; mild tilt/perspective fixable from plate rectangle; missing origin partly fixable; missing front line / under-loaded reference / overloading streaks never fixable; glare-blur-low-res rarely fixable (re-shoot instead)

Known real-plate defects catalogued (p6): MEHQ-P33 no front + faint Std; T-30min good lines/header but streaked lanes; E-30min S bleeds into A2; IMG_0450 plate tiny in frame, duplicate unnamed HEIC/DNG files
deep_read_reason: Full text of all 7 pages already extracted; every rule, number, and table is captured in the key points. Nothing remains beyond the two page-2 diagrams (Rf = a/b illustration), which add no new parameters.

title: The TLC plate reading system — Design, Visual Edition (Mstack Chemicals, prepared by Tejas Ghatule)
two_line_summary: Author's own 10-page stage-by-stage design of the TLC pipeline (GATE→NORMALIZE→STRUCTURE→CONVERT→EXTRACT→CORRELATE→CONCLUDE), each stage illustrated with real lab plates and actual prototype outputs. Carries concrete rules, thresholds, and a validation scorecard (T-30, P33, P32) that the brief's 15 findings do not fully cover.
key_points: Pipeline is 7 stages: GATE (real plate?), NORMALIZE (flat & clean), STRUCTURE (lines/lanes), CONVERT (plate→graph), EXTRACT (spots & curves), CORRELATE (rules), CONCLUDE (verdicts + %) — p.1

Only two hard rejections allowed in the whole system: 'not a TLC plate' or 'not workable', decided upfront with named reason; ugly-but-genuine plates are never refused, penalties go into confidence scores — p.1-2
Gate checks (all image-computed): UV-green background, low texture, lane-like structure, enough pixels, focus — p.2
Normalize: OpenCV segmentation + perspective warp, orientation from text/dot signals, iterative background fit → OD (absorbance) signal — p.3

Structure: lane count measured never assumed; drawn origin line found through spotting dots; virtual origin fitted when missing; lane roles resolve lexicon→behaviour→one-tap user question saved forever; 'S' never assumed to mean anything — p.4
Convert: pixel-for-pixel plate→graph on calibrated Rf ruler; three layers: pixel (trust view), curve (per-lane intensity, where correlations run), interpreted (classifications) — p.5

Extract: lane curves → matched-filter peaks → sub-pixel GAUSSIAN fits with per-spot SNR (NOTE: brief says EMG peak model — brief supersedes this detail); 2-tier confirmed/candidate reporting; cross-lane stacking rescues sub-threshold repeats; SM impurities detected at 3-6 sigma — p.6
Rule 1 matrix shift: delta measured two ways (anchor + whole-curve alignment); methods must agree or delta=0 with widened tolerance; guard fired on P33 (weak co-spot signal at 158 px) — p.7, p.10
Rule 2 reference anchoring: anchors only from confirmed >=3-sigma reference spots, never the origin zone — p.7
Rule 3 impurity inheritance: present in S and Co, absent in Std → SM baggage not reaction by-product (action: purify SM, not route) — p.7
Rule 4 co-spot decomposition: Co ≈ alpha·S + beta·R fitted; R² is plate self-consistency score; on T-30: Co = 0.35·S + 0.99·R, R² = 0.83 — p.7, p.10
Rule 5 conflict resolution: position matching two anchors decided by intensity consistency (example: 1.89 ≈ Std's 2.18 vs impurity's 0.07 → 'product') — p.7
Rule 6 streak guard: lanes with >55% of lane above noise report zones only, % withheld; fired on all four T-30 condition lanes, prevented false '100% conversion' — p.7, p.10

Rule 7: apparent conversion = product:SM within one lane (UV caveat); series verdicts across timepoints via delta-SM/delta-product + zone accounting → progressing/stalled/complete/degrading; P32 4hr→7hr product-zone +10 pts → 'progressing' at low confidence (93 px sources) — p.7, p.10

Confidence formula: match score = both spots' detection strength × position agreement × delta-quality; verdict score = weakest link in its evidence chain; High=stated, Medium=stated with caveat, Low=system asks instead of asserting — p.9

No front line → no Rf; no calibration → apparent % only; blank/everything-at-front/co-running-references plates get named 'cannot conclude, because…' — p.9 (consistent with brief's Rst finding, but Rf WAS computed on T-30 where drawn lines existed)

Determinism requirement: no randomness, temperature 0 with pinned models for text reading, outputs quantized with hysteresis so boundary values can't flip verdicts; verified two full T-30 runs byte-identical JSON, hash 49d796a8… — p.9

LLM boundary (hard requirement): LLMs used for exactly two things — reading handwriting (classical OCR fails on marker cursive, tested) and one cached schema-constrained tie-break call for ambiguous lane names; never for spot detection, correlations, or verdicts — p.9

Validation scorecard: plate finding+warp 6/6 plates incl. 77 px and tilted; structure perfect on T-30 (6 lanes + both pencil lines) but adaptive tuning still needed on 3 plates → user lane-map fallback path; averaging across lane gives sqrt(N) noise win — p.6, p.10

Output is a 3-page report: page 1 answers pointed at highlighted plate bands, pages 2-3 finding cards, densitograms, expert table; every user-flagged wrong result joins a golden regression suite — p.8-9
Named plates/params: T-30 (6 lanes, drawn lines, 536 px crisp source), P33 (158 px archive), P32 (93 px, 4hr/7hr series); photo resolution directly determines graph quality — p.5, p.10
deep_read_reason: The document is image-dominant — every stage shows real input plates and actual prototype outputs (annotated structure detection, Rf-ruler graphs, densitograms, the report page) that text extraction cannot capture; a builder should view the pages visually. Also needs reconciliation with the brief on two tensions: Gaussian fits here vs EMG in the brief, and Rf computed on T-30 vs the brief's no-solvent-front/Rst finding.

title: System Flow — How the TLC reading system works (Mstack Chemicals, Tejas Ghatule)
two_line_summary: Internal 7-page plain-language spec of the full pipeline: Flow A (single plate: detect, straighten, illumination-normalize, lanes/origin/front, EMG-style spot fitting) and Flow B (reaction time series: align via reference lanes, compare, verdict). Also enumerates 16 edge cases with required behaviors and 5 stated system limits — this is a behavioral requirements doc, not a research paper.
key_points: Flow A pipeline order (p.2): read raw photo unmodified (no brighten/sharpen) -> crop only if plate sits in wider bench photo -> find plate as brightest green region, read 4 corners -> edge-strip check: inspect thin strip just OUTSIDE each detected edge; if it still looks like plate, widen the boundary (anti-clipping guard) -> perspective-straighten via 4 corners -> estimate plate's own blank illumination field -> convert each pixel to darkness relative to that field (exposure-invariant) -> mask non-measured regions (warp frame, heading, lane labels) as greyed-out but visible -> lanes/origin/front -> per-lane curve, fit every bump for position, width, amount, each with uncertainty

Line placement rules (p.2, p.6): lane count comes from lane labels/user; origin from spotting dots, fallback to lane-label row with reduced confidence; front from drawn pencil line if present, else a 'working line' placed just above the highest spot with scale labelled 'apparent' (matches brief's Rst-not-Rf finding)

Single-plate output contract (p.3): the graph (full converted plate, nothing cropped), two lines (dashed origin; blue front — solid if pencil-found, dotted if working line), spot table per lane (position, share of lane signal, width, confidence), answers (SM gone? product formed? inherited impurities?), and explicit warnings (no front line, low resolution, overexposed, streaky lane)
Repeatability requirement (p.3): same photo must produce byte-for-byte identical output, verified by running plates twice

Flow B (p.4): each timepoint runs Flow A independently (bad photo doesn't spoil others); cross-plate alignment uses reference lanes containing the same material on every plate; changes measured as differences with uncertainty

Four verdicts with definitions (p.5): PROGRESSING = SM falling and product rising by more than measurement uncertainty; STALLED = 2+ intervals with no real change; COMPLETE = SM at/below detection limit and product steady; DEGRADING = product shrinking or new spots growing while product falls

Series report contents (p.5): timepoint strip on one scale, conversion table with uncertainty per timepoint and deltas, new-spot flags, inherited-impurity flags (present from first plate), rate estimate labelled as estimate only when trend is steady

Edge-case behaviors, single plate (p.6): not-a-plate rejected with reason and measured value; blank plate -> 'no spots found'; overexposed -> quantities switched OFF (not degraded); plate partially outside frame -> positions along cut direction marked unreliable, Rf switched off if cut at top/bottom; streaked lane -> percentages withheld, likely cause reported (overloading, acid-base effect, decomposition); merged spots -> reported as one spot with width-suggests-two note and weaker-solvent suggestion; unfamiliar lane names -> ask once via dropdown, remember per lab; small/blurry photo -> analyse anyway with all confidences capped and resolution limit stated

Edge-case behaviors, series (p.6): missing timepoint shown as gap, never interpolated; different solvents -> refuse trend; changed lane layout -> compare only same-role lanes; no times recorded -> upload order, no time axis; non-monotonic conversion -> no smoothing, report as no-real-change if inside uncertainty; single usable plate -> fall back to single-plate report

Stated limits (p.7): percentages are of signal not moles (calibrated reference spots would make exact); true Rf requires drawn origin+front lines else 'apparent'; two spots closer than ~5% of plate height cannot be separated on a small photo; clipped overexposure unrecoverable; lane count on low-res photos must come from the user (asked once, remembered)

Trust/traceability requirements (p.7): every finding marked on the graph for visual confirmation; confidence built from named factors (photo quality, front drawn, spot strength); every run replayable — each stage stores input, decision, and reason; chemist-flagged wrong results become permanent regression test cases

Doc is authored by the user (Tejas Ghatule, Mstack Chemicals) and is consistent with the brief's 15 findings (raw-photo handling, exposure clipping unrecoverable, apparent positions without front, ensemble-of-named-factors confidence); no contradictions found
deep_read_reason: All 7 pages were fully text-extracted during indexing; the key_points above capture every concrete rule, threshold, and behavior. The only content not extracted is the figures (example plate images on pages 3-4), which carry no additional parameters.
